sources.title: Report on the Loss of the "Titanic" (s.s.)
sources.publisher: His Majesty's Stationery Office; transcription by the Titanic Inquiry Project
sources.note: Sections read: Description of the Ship, Watertight Compartments, Decks and Accommodation, Structure, Life-saving Appliances, Machinery, Electrical Installation, Speed, Weather Conditions, The Collision, Extent of the Damage, Flooding in the First Ten Minutes, Gradual and Final Effect of the Damage, The Boats, Means Taken to Procure Assistance, Rescue by the Carpathia, Numbers Saved, Circumstances in Connection with the Californian.

sources.title: British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry, minutes of evidence
sources.publisher: Transcription by the Titanic Inquiry Project
sources.note: Read directly: Lee (Day 4), Stone and Gibson (Day 7), Boxhall (Day 13), Bride (Day 14), Rowe (Day 15), Wilding (Days 18 and 19). Other witnesses are cited by question number through the analyses that quote them; the note of each record says which.

sources.title: "Titanic" Disaster: Report of the Committee on Commerce, United States Senate
authors: United States Senate, Committee on Commerce (Senator William Alden Smith)
sources.publisher: Government Printing Office; transcription by the Titanic Inquiry Project
sources.note: Sections on the collision, flooding, distress calls, vessels in the vicinity, lifeboats, the sinking and the numbers on board and saved.

sources.title: United States Senate Inquiry, hearings
authors: United States Senate, Committee on Commerce
sources.publisher: Transcription by the Titanic Inquiry Project
sources.note: Read directly: Rostron (Day 1). Other witnesses are cited by transcript page through the analyses that quote them.

sources.title: Chronology of Events with References and Notes (revised 28 March 2023)
sources.publisher: titanicology.com; first published in the Centennial Reappraisal (2011)
sources.note: Read from 11:30 p.m. on 14 April to 9:00 a.m. on 15 April, with its notes. Uses Halpern's own lifeboat times.

sources.title: Lifeboats, Launch Times, List and Trim, Parts I and II
sources.note: Part II read in full (trim and list control points, launch table); Part I read in part.

sources.title: Angles of Trim and Heel (revised August 2017)
sources.note: Observation-based reconstruction of trim and heel, with an appendix on flooding observations.

sources.title: Titanic's List at 2:05 AM
sources.note: Also the route by which the positions of Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt on list and trim are known here.

sources.title: Finding the Apparent Floatation Pivot Point (AFPP)
sources.note: Tabulates the Hackett and Bedford flooding conditions and derives the pivot point of the waterline.

sources.title: Titanic's Initial List to Starboard
sources.note: Heeling-moment calculation for the early starboard list.

sources.title: A Matter of Stability and Trim
sources.note: Hull coefficients and hydrostatic particulars taken from Harland and Wolff records.

sources.title: Somewhere About 12 Square Feet
sources.note: Re-derivation of Wilding's estimate of the aggregate opening and of inflow rates.

sources.title: Titanic's Master of Time (second print, 10 November 2019)
sources.note: Ship's clocks, the planned setback and the argument that no setback was made before the collision.

sources.title: 1 Hour and 33 Minutes: A Time Difference Gone Wrong
sources.note: Origin of the 1 h 33 min ship-to-New-York difference used in 1912.

sources.title: It May Have Been a Dozen or It May Have Been More
sources.note: Number and timing of the distress signals; alignment of Titanic and Californian clocks.

sources.title: Signals of Distress: What Color Were They? (revised February 2021)
sources.note: Type, stock, firing position and colour of the socket distress signals.

sources.title: Collision Point
sources.note: Collision and stopping positions, local current, heading after the collision, wreck coordinates.

sources.title: Report into the Loss of the SS Titanic: A Centennial Reappraisal
sources.note: Not consulted directly. Reached through Halpern's online articles and through page references given by Wikipedia.

sources.title: The Sinking of S.S. Titanic: Investigated by Modern Techniques
sources.note: Flooding conditions C0 to C7 are taken from Halpern's tabulation; the paper itself was not obtained.

sources.title: Titanic: The Lifeboat Launching Sequence, A New Study (version 1.4, May 2026) and its chart "Launch Times Re-Examined, 2026 Version"
sources.note: Chart read in full; in the study, the introduction and the final summary of findings were read and the rest searched by keyword.

sources.title: Titanic: The Lifeboat Launching Sequence Re-Examined (2001, revised to February 2023), with its Tables 1 and 2
sources.publisher: wormstedt.com; originally The Titanic Commutator no. 155
sources.note: Sections on the distress rockets, the first lifeboat, the combined sequence and the collapsibles; Table 1 reproduces the British Inquiry times.

sources.title: Titanic: A Desperate Dialogue
sources.note: Collation of the wireless logs (procès-verbaux) of the ships and shore stations, kept in New York time or GMT.

sources.title: The Breakup of Titanic: A Progress Report from the Marine Forensics Panel (SD-7)
sources.publisher: Society of Naval Architects and Marine Engineers; later in Marine Technology (2010)
sources.note: Reference model of the break-up used by this project. The 2010 journal version was not consulted.

sources.title: The Wreck of RMS Titanic: "The Break-up of Titanic" and "The bow section"
sources.note: Break-up sequence, state of the two sections and descent of the bow.

sources.title: RMS "Titanic": Reappraisal of Evidence Relating to SS "Californian"
authors: Marine Accident Investigation Branch (James de Coverly, Thomas Barnett)
sources.note: Text layer of the scan read; some longitudes are illegible in it and were confirmed through Halpern's quotations.

sources.title: Titanic: First ever full-sized scans reveal wreck as never seen before
sources.note: First report of the 2022 Magellan and Atlantic Productions scan.

sources.title: Press coverage of "Titanic: The Digital Resurrection" (National Geographic and Atlantic Productions, April 2025)
sources.publisher: BBC News; Smithsonian Magazine; National Geographic
sources.note: Read through summarising fetches and search results, not as raw pages. Figures for the scan (715,000 photographs, 16 terabytes, two remotely operated vehicles) are consistent across outlets; the duration of data collection is given as three, four or six weeks.

sources.title: Archaeology of Titanic
sources.note: Account of the 2010 mapping expedition and of the site.

sources.title: The Quest to Map Titanic
sources.note: Interview on the 2010 survey vehicles and methods.

sources.title: The Discovery of the Titanic
sources.note: Not consulted directly. Cited through Halpern, the MAIB report and page references given by Wikipedia.

sources.title: Titanic
sources.note: The site refused direct requests; its statements were read through search-result extracts of its own pages (bow coordinates, casualty figures attributed to the two inquiries).

sources.title: Titanic statistics
sources.note: The site refused direct requests; totals were read through a search-result extract of its table and agree with the Titanic International Society fact sheet.

sources.title: The Loss of the S.S. Titanic
sources.note: Survivor account, read through a summarising fetch; wording is paraphrased, not quoted.

sources.title: "Titanic", "Sinking of the Titanic", "Wreck of the Titanic", "Lifeboats of the Titanic", "Iceberg that sank the Titanic" and "SS Californian"
sources.note: Tertiary source, used only as a pointer to published works and for a few commonly quoted figures not found in the primary sources read; records relying on it are never marked established on its strength alone.

sources.title: Did small holes in hull doom Titanic?
sources.note: Press account of the 1996 sonar survey of the buried bow, read through a summarising fetch.

sources.title: 1/350 Titanic funnels (product page citing the Harland and Wolff rigging plan)
sources.note: Weak source, used only for the rake of the funnels, whose arithmetic was checked.

sources.title: Bright Star Catalogue, 5th Revised Edition (preliminary version), VizieR catalogue V/50
sources.publisher: Yale University Observatory; Centre de Données astronomiques de Strasbourg
sources.note: Positions (J2000), proper motions, visual magnitudes and B−V colours of the stars brighter than about magnitude 6.5.

sources.title: Astronomy Engine
sources.note: MIT-licensed ephemeris library (VSOP87 and NOVAS-based) used to compute the positions of the Sun, Moon and planets and the orientation of the sky.

sources.title: Derivations and estimates made by the Titanic 4D project
sources.note: Used when a value is computed or interpolated by the project from other cited records. The method is stated in the note of each record, and such records are never marked established.
